title: Introduce commitment-hedger and soft spillover proxy for dedicated fleets
author: Sofia Liu
release_notes: Adds a CommitmentHedger controller and a soft-spillover proxy to improve throughput stability for dedicated fleets under bursty load. Backward-compatible; configurable via FleetSpec.commitmentHedger. Rollout: gradual canary (10/50/100%).
description: Context: customers with reserved dedicated capacity experience transient demand bursts that either overload the pool or force aggressive evictions, causing tail-latency spikes and SLA violations. Motivation: provide a soft, reversible mechanism that 1) keeps a small escrow of capacity per-tenant (hedge) to smooth short spikes, 2) proactively routes excess bursts to defined spillover destinations (other pools or lower-cost model variants) without hard preemption, and 3) emit actionable telemetry to reason about commitment health and spill decisions. Summary of changes: implemented a new controller (CommitmentHedger) that maintains per-tenant escrow balances using a time-decayed ledger and probabilistic top-ups based on recent utilization and commitment history; added a lightweight proxy (soft-spillover-proxy) that intercepts admission checks and, when hedger balance is depleted, attempts spill routing according to a configurable policy (preferred-pools, fallback-models, degrade-to-disk). The proxy supports rate-limited burst routing and respects tenant SLAs. Telemetry: hedger.escrow_balance, hedger.util_delta_1m, hedger.topup_events, spillover.routed_count, spillover.drop_count, spillover.target_latency_estimate. Config: FleetSpec.commitmentHedger{enabled, target_escrow_percent, decay_half_life_seconds, max_topup_per_minute} and FleetSpec.spilloverPolicy{priority_targets, latency_safety_margin, max_spill_rate}. Safety: soft decisions only — no forced evictions. Hedger exposes a graceful drain hook for planful decommissioning. Tests & validation: unit tests for ledger math and decay semantics; integration e2e in staging with synthetic bursts; load test across two canary pools (eu-west-1a, us-east-1b) with 48-hour stability windows. Observed results in staging: 95th latency unchanged (+1ms median variance), dropped eviction count reduced by 62% during bursts, spillover routed 7.3% of peak traffic with tail latency within SLA. Performance overhead: proxy adds ~0.7ms p99 admission latency. Rollout plan: canary 10% (48h) -> 50% (72h) -> 100% (gradual); keep hedger target_escrow_percent default to 3% for first month. Guides: added docs to redwood/docs/fleet/commitment-hedger.md and a console toggle with telemetry graphs. Related: ENG-3146 (design doc), SUP-1287 (customer incident reproduction).
